scope: First deployment batch enablement for the CloudIdentity owner (services/gateway-integration, owner tenant). Source and focused PostgreSQL verification only: no service was deployed, no Instance manifest was changed, no provider or money mutation ran.

problem.statement: The owner that answers CloudIdentity authorization installed a failing cloud_identity readiness check for itself whenever OPL_CLOUD_IDENTITY_URL was absent and a database was present, so it could never report SERVING in an installation that had not deployed a separate authority.

reproduction.shape: tenant owner, real isolated PostgreSQL database, OPL_CLOUD_IDENTITY_URL unset, TenantProductService group registered
reproduction.observedBefore: FAIL: tenant: dependency cloud_identity is not ready: CloudIdentity authorization is not configured
reproduction.observedAfter: PASS: the authority reports Ready and SERVING

problem.secondStatement: The Build owner-commit readback dialed its target unconditionally. grpc.NewClient accepts an empty target without error, so an unconfigured OPL_BUILD_ADDR installed a client whose failure surfaced later as an unrelated transport error instead of an explicit absence. The Workspace readback in the same process already guarded on a non-empty address.

sourceEvidence.fact: The readiness check was installed without excluding the owner that answers authorization
sourceEvidence.after: the same check is installed only when config.Owner != OwnerTenant

sourceEvidence.fact: Every owner resolves the CloudIdentity address from OPL_CLOUD_IDENTITY_URL, and an absent address yields an authorizer with no client

The authority's own members path authorizes in-process through Service.AuthorizeAction, not through the ownerservice.Authorizer, so the batch-1 login/session/invitation flow does not depend on a configured address
The Build readback dialed without an address guard while the Workspace readback guarded
sourceEvidence.after: Build and Workspace are wired through one guarded loop: no address, no client

sourceEvidence.fact: The tenant owner is the CloudIdentity authority and the only target service that registers the authorization server

implementation.ownerservice: The cloud_identity readiness check now applies to every owner except the authority. The change is a precondition on an existing check; no new check, gate or fallback was added.
implementation.gateway-integration: Build and Workspace owner-commit readback share one guarded wiring loop. A configured address dials and tracks the connection; an absent address leaves the corresponding grant path refusing rather than installing a client against an empty target.
implementation.configuration: docs/runtime/package-buildkit-local.md records the absence rule where OPL_BUILD_ADDR is already documented as canonical configuration.
implementation.test: services/internal/ownerservice/readiness_postgres_test.go gains TestCloudIdentityAuthorityDoesNotRequireASeparateCloudIdentity, which pins both directions against a real PostgreSQL server: the authority serves without dialing itself, and an ordinary owner is still gated on a configured address.

focusedVerification.command: OPL_OWNER_MIGRATION_TEST_ADMIN_DSN=<isolated loopback admin DSN> go -C services/internal/ownerservice test -run TestCloudIdentityAuthorityDoesNotRequireASeparateCloudIdentity -count=1 -v
focusedVerification.coverage: authority subtest: Ready and SERVING with no configured address; gated subtest: an owner without a configured address reports Ready error naming cloud_identity and does not report SERVING

focusedVerification.command: OPL_OWNER_MIGRATION_TEST_ADMIN_DSN=<isolated loopback admin DSN> go -C services/internal/ownerservice test ./... -count=1
focusedVerification.coverage: the whole shared owner-process package against real PostgreSQL, including the pre-existing readiness and operation over-the-wire tests

focusedVerification.command: OPL_OWNER_MIGRATION_TEST_ADMIN_DSN=<isolated loopback admin DSN> go -C services/gateway-integration test ./... -count=1
focusedVerification.coverage: identity, migrations and the command package; member governance, repository binding and workspace grant persistence tests unchanged
ordinary source verification across contracts, control-plane, fabric, ledger and shared packages

focusedVerification.command: gofmt -l services/internal/ownerservice services/gateway-integration; go vet ./... in both modules
focusedVerification.coverage: formatting and static analysis for both changed modules

remainingGaps.gap: The authority's own shared OwnerOperations group still cannot authorize without a configured CloudIdentity address.
remainingGaps.evidence: With owner tenant, a real database and no address, ownerservice.Authorizer.Authorize returns 'Unavailable: CloudIdentity authorization is not configured' after the scope check passes.
remainingGaps.whyNotFixedHere: Resolving it requires the authority to answer authorization in-process from its own store. The policy implementation lives in gateway-integration while the authorizer is constructed inside the shared startup path before the owner's own service exists, so the fix changes the shared startup contract for every owner. It is a distinct outcome and is not smuggled into this change.
remainingGaps.affectedPath: console operation readback /api/v2/operations/{owner}/{operationId} for owner=tenant, not the batch-1 login, session and invitation flow
remainingGaps.note: This gap was reproduced but is not pinned as expected behaviour in any test.

notProven: That services/gateway-integration runs in the Instance unit or reports SERVING on Tencent/TKE.
That any CloudIdentity-authorized call from another owner succeeds in a deployed installation.
That the Console BFF session surface is reachable or switched.
Any Instance receipt: this change produces no deployment, rollout, rollback or provider qualification evidence.
